extra_misconceptions.fact: Friction shatters ice crystals inside frozen cells and destroys tissue; warm frostbite gently in 99 to 102 degree F water.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Rubbing frostbitten skin vigorously with hands or snow restores blood circulation safely to frozen toes.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Doubled cotton socks trap moisture, bunch up, and create friction blisters; wear one snug pair of moisture-wicking socks.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wearing two pairs of thick cotton socks inside skates prevents heel blisters and keeps feet warmer on ice.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Catching full body weight on stiff, unguarded hands frequently fractures the wrist; wear rigid wrist guards when roller or inline skating.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Bracing a forward fall with outstretched bare hands protects the skater from serious upper-body injury.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Intact skin acts as a sterile barrier against bacteria; cover small blisters with a moleskin doughnut pad instead of puncturing them.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Popping a friction blister on the heel with an unsterilized pin lets a skater return to the rink safely.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to rub frostbitten fingers or toes with snow instead of rewarming them in lukewarm water?
Which physical indicator distinguishes severe hypothermia from mild cold stress when checking a skater outdoors?
What water temperature range confirms safe rapid rewarming for a frostbitten foot without causing thermal burn damage?
Where should a Scout position sterile gauze and direct pressure if a skate blade causes a deep lower-leg laceration?

extra_misconceptions.fact: White snow ice contains trapped air pockets and has only about half the strength of clear new ice, requiring double the thickness.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Milky white snow ice has the same load-bearing strength as clear blue lake ice of equal thickness.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Moisture trapped against steel blades causes rapid rusting and pitting; wipe blades completely dry with a cloth before storing them.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Storing wet ice skates inside plush fabric soakers or a closed gym bag prevents blade rust overnight.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Standing near thin ice concentrates weight and breaks the edge; rescuers must stay on shore or lie flat to distribute weight with a pole.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Walking upright out onto the edge of an ice hole is the fastest way to pull a fallen skater out of freezing water.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Flat blades simply slide backward without grip; skaters must push outward at an angle against the inside edge to generate forward thrust.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pushing straight backward with a flat skate blade or wheel generates forward propulsion on a skating rink.

extra_socratic_questions: What measurement confirms that clear, newly formed natural ice is thick enough to support a small group of skaters safely?
Where should a Scout position their body weight and hands when extending a weighted rescue line to a skater through the ice?
What happens to your turning radius and stability if your trailing skate fails to push on its outside edge during a crossover?
Under what condition does walking across concrete without hard skate guards ruin the hollow grind of an ice skate blade?
